2: The Strongest Sage with the Weakest Crest by Shinkoshoto (Square Enix) is a fantasy adventure about a hero starting over on purpose. The greatest sage of his age was born with a crest poorly suited to magic, so he reincarnates far in the future to get a better one. He wakes as young Matthias, only to find that magic has badly declined in his absence. It's a fun, fast read for fans of overpowered heroes and reincarnation stories.
3: Pandora in the Crimson Shell by Masamune Shirow (Seven Seas) is a lighthearted sci-fi action story from the creator of Ghost in the Shell. Nene Nanakorobi, a cheerful girl with a full cyborg body, travels to the island city of Seranos. There she meets Clarion, a gynoid with a prickly attitude, and the two become unlikely partners. Expect cute character moments mixed with cyberpunk tech and action.
5: Faerie's Landing by You Hyun (Tokyopop) is a Korean fantasy romance with a big dose of comedy. High school student Ryang Jegal's ordinary life changes when Faerie Goodfellow, a fairy exiled from her own world, lands in his. Faerie must live among humans while she works off her punishment, and Ryang gets pulled into the chaos. It's a charming pick for readers who like folklore mixed with school-life humor.
6: Black God by Dall-Young Lim (Yen Press) is a supernatural action series with a touch of romance. Keita Ibuki's life takes a strange turn when he meets Kuro, a powerful girl who guards the balance of the world. Their meeting draws Keita into a hidden struggle tied to people's doppelgangers and the luck they share. It's a good fit for readers who enjoy contract-partner battles and urban fantasy.
7: Rebound by Yuriko Nishiyama (Tokyopop) is a high-energy basketball series and the follow-up to her Harlem Beat. Nate Torres and his teammates at Johnan High chase their dream of winning at the national level. Along the way they face tough rivals, fierce games, and plenty of locker-room comedy. It's a great pick for sports manga fans who love team chemistry and fast-paced court action.
8: High School DxD by Ichiei Ishibumi (Yen Press) is a comedic action fantasy light novel with plenty of fan service. Issei Hyodo, a hopelessly girl-crazy high schooler, finally gets a date, only for her to turn out to be a fallen angel who kills him. He's brought back to life by Rias Gremory, a beautiful upperclassman who is secretly a devil, and becomes her servant. It's for readers who like harem comedy mixed with supernatural battles.
10: Gantz by Hiroya Oku (Dark Horse) is an intense sci-fi action series for mature readers. High schooler Kei Kurono and his old friend Masaru Kato are killed by a subway train. They wake up in an apartment with a mysterious black sphere, along with other people who just died. The sphere sends them out to hunt aliens in a deadly game. It's violent and gripping, made for readers who like survival stories with high stakes.
13: Sensual Phrase by Mayu Shinjo (Viz Media) is a steamy shojo romance set in the music world. High school student Aine Sakurazaka dreams of writing song lyrics. When she meets Sakuya, the lead singer of the hit rock band Lucifer, he takes an interest in both her words and her. Their romance pulls her into the glamorous, complicated world of fame. It's for older teen readers who love dramatic, passionate love stories.
14: Tomb Raider King by San.G (Ize Press) is a Korean action fantasy about a second chance. When mysterious tombs appeared across the world, the relics inside gave people incredible powers. Seo Jooheon spent his life raiding tombs for others, only to be betrayed and killed. Now he's back fifteen years in the past, determined to claim every relic for himself. It's a fast, satisfying read for fans of regression stories and treasure hunting.
16: Battle Vixens by Yuji Shiozaki (Tokyopop) is a martial arts action series with lots of fan service. Its fighters carry magatama beads that bind them to the fates of warriors from China's Three Kingdoms era. Hakufu Sonsaku, a cheerful and powerful fighter, transfers to Nanyo Academy and is quickly drawn into the battles between rival schools. It's for readers who enjoy nonstop brawls and a playful twist on classic history.
19: Sayonara, Football by Naoshi Arakawa (Kodansha) is a heartfelt sports story from the creator of Your Lie in April. Nozomi Onda is a talented soccer player who has always held her own against the boys. Now in middle school, she is told that she can't play in official games with the boys' team. Determined to prove herself, she keeps fighting for a spot on the field. It's an inspiring read for anyone who loves an underdog.
21: Maria Holic by Minari Endou (Tokyopop) is an offbeat school comedy. Kanako Miyamae breaks out in hives whenever a boy touches her, so she transfers to an all-girls Catholic school hoping to find true love. There she meets Mariya Shidou, a stunning student who seems perfect. Kanako soon learns that Mariya is really a sharp-tongued boy in disguise, and she's forced to keep his secret. It's for readers who like snappy, slightly twisted humor.
23: Switch by naked ape (Viz Media) is a gritty crime action series with a mystery at its core. Kai Eto, a sweet-natured rookie, joins a special narcotics unit and is partnered with the sharp, tough Hal Etoh. Together they go undercover to take down drug dealers and the dangerous groups behind them. As the cases grow darker, the partners' own secrets start to surface. It's a good pick for fans of buddy cops and tense drama.
34: Toppu GP by Kosuke Fujishima (Kodansha) is a motorcycle racing story from the creator of Oh My Goddess! Toppu Bando has loved racing since he was a kid and dreams of competing at the very top of the sport. The series follows his rise through the racing world as he faces rivals, setbacks, and the thrill of speed. It's a great fit for readers who enjoy sports stories full of mechanical detail and drive.
38: Reborn as a Space Mercenary by Ryuto (Seven Seas) is a sci-fi adventure light novel. A gamer wakes up inside the world of his favorite space simulation game, along with his powerful starship, the Krishna. Now going by Hiro, he decides to make a living as a mercenary, fighting pirates and taking jobs across the stars. He soon picks up a crew of his own. It's a fun read for fans of isekai with a space-opera twist.
39: Reincarnated as a Dragon Hatchling by Nekoko (Seven Seas) is a fantasy adventure light novel. After dying, the hero is reborn in a dangerous fantasy world as a newly hatched dragon. He's small, weak, and surrounded by monsters, so he has to fight, level up, and evolve to survive. Along the way he tries to hold on to his human heart. It's a good pick for readers who enjoy monster-reincarnation stories and growth-focused adventures.
41: Freezing by Dall-Young Lim (Seven Seas) is a sci-fi action series with plenty of fan service. Humanity's defenders against the alien Nova are the Pandoras, genetically enhanced young women, and their male partners, the Limiters. Kazuya Aoi arrives at West Genetics Academy and immediately crosses paths with Satellizer el Bridget, a powerful Pandora known as the Untouchable Queen. It's for readers who like intense battles and school rivalries with a dramatic edge.
44: The Hidden Dungeon Only I Can Enter by Meguru Seto (Seven Seas) is a fantasy adventure with comedy and fan service. Noir Stardia is the son of a low-ranking noble family with few prospects. Everything changes when he stumbles on a secret dungeon that no one else can enter, full of rare treasure and powerful skills. With its help he sets out to get stronger. It's for fans of dungeon-crawling stories and lighthearted harem comedy.
45: The Kingdoms of Ruin by Yoruhashi (Seven Seas) is a dark fantasy about revenge. In a world where humans have turned against magic, the witch Chloe is hunted down and killed. Her devoted apprentice, Adonis, survives and vows to make humanity pay. What follows is a bloody, emotional story of grief and vengeance. It's best for readers who like intense, morally gray fantasy with a tragic heart.
51: To Love Ru Darkness by Saki Hasemi (Seven Seas) is a romantic comedy with heavy fan service, and the sequel to To Love Ru. Rito Yuki's home is already crowded with alien princesses. Now Momo, one of Lala's younger sisters, has a plan to build Rito a harem, while the assassin Golden Darkness wrestles with her feelings about him. It's for fans of the original who want more chaotic, cheeky comedy.
52: Precarious Woman Executive Miss Black General by Jin (Seven Seas) is a goofy action comedy that pokes fun at superhero shows. The Black General is a top executive in an evil organization that keeps losing to a team of heroes. Her biggest problem? She has fallen for Akagi, the red-suited leader of the heroes she's supposed to be fighting. It's a light, silly read for anyone who enjoys tokusatsu parodies and romantic comedy.
53: Rainbows After Storms by Luka Kobachi (Viz Media) is a sweet yuri romance about two high school girls. Chidori is cool and reserved, while Nijiko is warm and cheerful, and the two are close friends. As they spend more time together, their friendship slowly grows into something more. It's a gentle, heartfelt read for anyone who loves slow-building school romances.
54: Durarara!! by Ryohgo Narita (Yen Press) is an urban fantasy light novel with a big cast and lots of mystery. Mikado Ryugamine moves to Ikebukuro, a lively Tokyo district buzzing with rumors of street gangs, an online group called the Dollars, and a headless rider on a black motorcycle. Soon Mikado learns that some of the rumors are true. It's a great pick for readers who like interwoven stories and quirky characters.
60: Bloody Cross by Shiwo Komeyama (Yen Press) is a dark fantasy action series. Tsukimi is half angel and half vampire, and she carries a curse that will kill her before long. Her only hope is to find a powerful grimoire that might lift it. Along the way, she crosses paths with Hinata, another half-breed with the same curse and his own reasons for wanting the book. It's for fans of supernatural battles and uneasy alliances.
64: Like a Butterfly by Suu Morishita (Viz Media) is a gentle shojo romance. Suiren Shiraishi is so beautiful that people rarely see past her looks, and she is too shy to make real connections. Then she meets Taichi Kawasaki, a quiet, blunt classmate who treats her like anyone else. Slowly the two begin to open up to each other. It's a sweet, low-drama read for fans of soft, slow-burn school romance.
65: Log Horizon: The West Wind Brigade by Koyuki (Yen Press) is a fantasy spin-off of Mamare Touno's Log Horizon. When thousands of players are trapped inside the online game Elder Tale, the skilled samurai Soujirou Seta leads the West Wind Brigade, a guild made up almost entirely of women who adore him. The series follows the guild's adventures and comedy in this new world. It's for Log Horizon fans who want a lighter side story.
66: Sankarea by Mitsuru Hattori (Kodansha) is a quirky romantic comedy with a zombie twist. Chihiro Furuya is a high school boy obsessed with zombie movies who is secretly working on a potion to bring his dead cat back to life. Then he meets Rea Sanka, a sheltered rich girl desperate to escape her overbearing father. When tragedy strikes, Chihiro's potion changes everything. It's a strange, sweet read for fans of offbeat romance.
67: Yakuza Lover by Nozomi Mino (Viz Media) is a dramatic shojo romance for older teens. College student Yuri is saved from an assault by a handsome stranger named Toshiomi Oya. She falls for him at once, only to learn that he is the heir to a powerful yakuza family. As their relationship grows, she's pulled into a dangerous world she never expected. It's for readers who enjoy intense, high-stakes love stories.
68: Lovesick Ellie by Fujimomo (Kodansha) is a funny, sweet shojo romantic comedy. Eleanor Ichimori is a plain, quiet high school girl who secretly posts wild fantasy stories online about the most popular boy in class, Akira Omi. Then Omi discovers her account. Instead of exposing her, he seems oddly interested in her. It's a cute pick for readers who love awkward heroines and a teasing romance.
69: Yu-Gi-Oh! 5D's by Masahiro Hikokubo and Masashi Sato (Viz Media) is a card-battle action series set in the Yu-Gi-Oh! world. In Neo Domino City, duelists face off in Turbo Duels, high-speed card battles fought on motorcycles. Yusei Fudo, a talented young duelist, enters the city's biggest tournament with his own reasons to win. It's a great pick for kids and fans of the anime who love fast-paced card battles.
70: Shortcake Cake by Suu Morishita (Viz Media) is a warm shojo romance set in a boarding house. Ten Nagamori moves into a boarding house so she won't have a long commute to high school. There she lives alongside several classmates, including the charming, outspoken Riku and the quiet, kind Chiaki. As they share daily life, feelings start to grow. It's a gentle, cozy read for fans of slice-of-life romance.
71: Show-ha Shoten! by Akinari Asakura and Takeshi Obata (Viz Media) is a comedy drama about the world of stand-up comedy. Taiyo Azuma is a shy high schooler who secretly writes jokes. Kouta Higashikata is a classmate with a big personality who wants to become a comedian. When the two team up as a comedy duo, they set out to make all of Japan laugh. It's an upbeat read for anyone who loves stories about chasing a dream.
74: Mushoku Tensei: Roxy Gets Serious by Rifujin na Magonote (Seven Seas) is a fantasy adventure spin-off of Mushoku Tensei. It follows Roxy Migurdia, the young demon-race mage who becomes Rudeus's beloved tutor. The story goes back to her own beginnings as she leaves her village, studies magic, and makes her way as an adventurer. It's a great pick for Mushoku Tensei fans who want to know more about one of its favorite characters.
75: Banished from the Hero's Party, I Decided to Live a Quiet Life in the Countryside by Zappon (Yen Press) is a cozy fantasy romance. Red was a member of the Hero's party until he was told he wasn't strong enough and pushed out. Instead of fighting back, he moves to a quiet frontier town to open an apothecary. Then Rit, a famous adventurer he once knew, shows up wanting to live with him. It's a sweet, relaxing read.
77: Kuma Kuma Kuma Bear by Kumanano (Seven Seas) is a lighthearted fantasy comedy. Yuna is a fifteen-year-old shut-in who spends her days playing a virtual reality game. One day she wakes up in a fantasy world, wearing a cute bear costume that turns out to be overpowered. Armed with her bear gear, she starts a new life as an adventurer. It's a cheerful, cozy read for anyone who enjoys gentle isekai stories.
78: Me & My Brothers by Hari Tokeino (Tokyopop) is a sweet shojo family comedy. After losing her parents, Sakura is raised by her four older stepbrothers, who all dote on her. As she grows up, she learns more about the family and the bonds that hold them together. It's a heartwarming, lighthearted read for fans of found family and gentle school-life stories.
79: Bungo Stray Dogs: Wan! by Kafka Asagiri and Neco Kanai (Yen Press) is a comedy spin-off of Bungo Stray Dogs. It shrinks the cast of the Armed Detective Agency and the Port Mafia into cute chibi versions. Instead of battles, the series focuses on silly everyday moments and gags. It's a fun, easygoing read for fans of the main series who want to see their favorite characters at play.
80: Plunderer by Suu Minazuki (Yen Press) is a fantasy action series with comedy and fan service. In Hina's world, everyone carries a Count, a number tied to something about their life that can decide their fate. Hina is traveling in search of the legendary Ace, one of the war heroes of the past. Her journey leads her to Licht, a goofy, perverted swordsman with a serious secret. It's for readers who enjoy action with a twist.
81: Farming Life in Another World by Kinosuke Naito (One Peace Books) is a relaxing fantasy slice-of-life story. Hiraku Machio dies after a long illness and is given a second chance in a new world, along with a divine farming tool. He settles in a remote forest and begins clearing land and growing crops. Before long, all kinds of people and creatures come to live with him. It's a calm, cozy pick for fans of village-building stories.
82: Mobile Suit Gundam: The Origin by Yoshikazu Yasuhiko (Vertical) is a sci-fi war drama that retells the original Gundam story. Yasuhiko, the character designer of the first series, revisits the One Year War between the Earth Federation and the Principality of Zeon. Young Amuro Ray climbs into the Gundam and is thrown into battle. The series also digs into the past of Char Aznable. It's a rich read for Gundam fans and lovers of mecha drama.
83: Stepping on Roses by Rinko Ueda (Viz Media) is a historical shojo romance set in Meiji-era Japan. Sumi Kitamura works hard to care for the orphans her brother keeps bringing home, but they're still deep in poverty. Then a wealthy young businessman, Soichiro Ashida, offers to marry her as a business arrangement. Sumi accepts, and must learn to live as a proper lady. It's for readers who love period dramas and contract-marriage romance.
84: Strike the Blood by Gakuto Mikumo (Yen Press) is a supernatural action series. Kojou Akatsuki is a high school student on Itogami Island, a city where demons and humans live side by side. He's also the Fourth Primogenitor, a legendary vampire. Yukina Himeragi, a young sword shaman, is sent to watch him and to stop him if he becomes a threat. It's for fans of vampire action with comedy and romance.
86: For the Kid I Saw in My Dreams by Kei Sanbe (Yen Press) is a dark crime thriller from the creator of Erased. As a boy, Mitsuo Senda lived through a nightmare when his family was attacked and his twin brother was taken. Years later, he's still searching for the people responsible. His hunt pulls him deep into a violent underworld. It's an intense, gripping read for mature fans of revenge stories and mysteries.
87: Full Metal Panic! by Shoji Gatoh (ADV) is an action comedy with mecha and romance. Sousuke Sagara is a teen soldier from the secret mercenary group Mithril. He's sent undercover to a Tokyo high school to protect Kaname Chidori, a girl who may hold dangerous secrets. Sousuke knows everything about war and nothing about normal teenage life, which leads to plenty of chaos. It's great for fans of action mixed with school comedy.
89: Afterschool Charisma by Kumiko Suekane (Viz Media) is a sci-fi mystery set at an unusual school. St. Kleio Academy is home to clones of famous historical figures, including Napoleon, Joan of Arc, and Mozart. Shiro Kamiya, the son of one of the school's teachers, is the only student who isn't a clone. When trouble starts on campus, the school's secrets come to light. It's for readers who like thoughtful sci-fi with a twist.
93: The Beginning After the End by TurtleMe (Yen Press) is a fantasy adventure about getting a second shot at life. King Grey ruled a world of great power and strength, but his life was lonely. After his death he's reborn in a world of magic and monsters as Arthur Leywin. With the memories of his old life, he sets out to grow stronger and do things differently this time. It's for fans of reincarnation stories and big fantasy worlds.
94: The Case Files of Jeweler Richard by Nanako Tsujimura (Seven Seas) is a gentle mystery light novel set around a jewelry shop. College student Seigi Nakata meets Richard, a striking British jeweler, while trying to sell an old ring. Seigi takes a part-time job at Richard's shop in Ginza, where every gem seems to come with a story. It's a warm, thoughtful read for fans of character-driven mysteries.
95: The Case Study of Vanitas by Jun Mochizuki (Yen Press) is a gothic fantasy adventure from the creator of Pandora Hearts. In a steampunk version of 19th-century Paris, the young vampire Noé meets Vanitas, a human who says he can cure vampires driven mad by a curse. The two set off together to save vampires and uncover the truth behind it. It's for readers who love stylish art and mysterious, morally gray heroes.
96: The Detective Is Already Dead by Nigozyu (Yen Press) is a mystery light novel with action and comedy. Kimihiko Kimizuka has a knack for getting caught up in trouble. Years ago he was the assistant to Siesta, a brilliant detective, and the two solved cases around the world together. Now Siesta is gone, and Kimihiko is trying to live a normal life, until new trouble finds him. It's for readers who enjoy sharp banter and mysteries.
97: The Drifting Classroom by Kazuo Umezz (Viz Media) is a classic horror survival story. Sho Takamatsu goes to school after a fight with his mom. Without warning, the entire school is transported to a strange, desolate wasteland. With no way home, the students and teachers must struggle to survive as fear and chaos take over. It's a gripping read for fans of vintage horror and survival stories.
98: New Lone Wolf and Cub by Kazuo Koike and Hideki Mori (Dark Horse) is a historical samurai drama and the continuation of Lone Wolf and Cub. Young Daigoro is left alone after the events of the original series. He is taken in by Togo Shigetaka, a master swordsman, and the two set out together on the road. It's a strong choice for fans of samurai tales and the classic original.
99: The Genius Prince's Guide to Raising a Nation Out of Debt by Toru Toba (Yen Press) is a fantasy comedy light novel about politics. Prince Wein of the small, struggling kingdom of Natra has to run the country while his father is ill. Wein would love to sell the country off and live a lazy life, but his clever schemes keep turning into successes. It's a fun pick for readers who enjoy strategy and scheming heroes.
